| **A Topos-Theoretic Bridge for Holographic Entanglement Entropy** | [arXiv:24XX.XXXXX](https://arxiv.org/abs/24XX.XXXXX)<br>Categories: quant-ph, math-ph, gr-qc<br>First Posted: 2025-MM-DD<br>Version: v1 | Preprint (arXiv)<br>Submitted to: PRX Quantum | Holographic Entanglement Entropy, Topos Theory, Quantum Gravity, Category Theory | We develop a topos-theoretic framework to unify holographic entanglement entropy calculations with quantum information theory. | **A Topos-Theoretic Bridge for Geometric Quantum Control** | [arXiv:24XX.XXXXX](https://arxiv.org/abs/24XX.XXXXX)<br>Categories: quant-ph, math.OC, cs.SY<br>First Posted: 2025-MM-DD<br>Version: v1 | Preprint (arXiv)<br>Submitted to: Journal of Mathematical Physics | Geometric Quantum Control, Topos Theory, Symplectic Geometry, Quantum Feedback | This work introduces a topos-theoretic approach to geometric quantum control by modeling quantum systems as sheaves over symplectic manifolds. We demonstrate that topos-theoretic localization enables robust control of quantum states under geometric perturbations, with applications to fault-tolerant quantum computing and quantum feedback networks. |
| **A Topos-Theoretic Bridge for Quantum Machine Learning** | [arXiv:24XX.XXXXX](https://arxiv.org/abs/24XX.XXXXX)<br>Categories: cs.LG, quant-ph, math-ph<br>First Posted: 2025-MM-DD<br>Version: v1 | Preprint (arXiv)<br>Submitted to: NeurIPS | Quantum Machine Learning, Topos Theory, Neural Networks, Topological Representation Learning | We establish a topos-theoretic bridge between category theory and quantum machine learning, proposing a new class of topological quantum neural networks (TQNNs). | **A Topos-Theoretic Bridge for Non-invertible Symmetry** | [arXiv:24XX.XXXXX](https://arxiv.org/abs/24XX.XXXXX)<br>Categories: quant-ph, math-ph, hep-th<br>First Posted: 2025-MM-DD<br>Version: v1 | Preprint (arXiv)<br>Submitted to: JHEP | Non-invertible Symmetry, Topos Theory, Quantum Field Theory, Topological Quantum Systems | We propose a topos-theoretic framework for describing non-invertible symmetries in quantum field theory, extending the categorical approach to include sheaf-theoretic representations of symmetry defects. Our construction unifies previous results on non-invertible duality and topological order, providing a rigorous mathematical foundation for analyzing symmetry-protected topological phases in higher-dimensional quantum systems. |
